clue.text: By which food may be conveyed in the stomach

definitions.text: By which food may be conveyed
definitions.meaning: a basket in which loaves are carried to the table
slang for the belly, where food ends up

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the container that carries loaves and an old slang term for the belly.

clue.text: One coming out is climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters are read upwards, so from bottom to top

parts.note: a debutante, DEB for short, is a young woman coming out into society

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a climbing plant is just coming out into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' looks like it describes the plant, but it tells you to read DEB upwards in this down light. 'Coming out' means a debutante's first entry into society, not a flower opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To bed out seedlings is to set them in the soil, so the verb is a synonym for putting in.

clue.text: Better fish — ten caught therein

indicators.note: therein says the following pieces sit inside the fish word

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is the Roman numeral for ten
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An angler's better fish has ten others caught inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To better someone is to outdo or surpass them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Much admired person, one of, mixed parentage?

definitions.meaning: someone treated almost as a god, a hero
in myth, a being with one divine parent and one human parent

explanation.definitionFit: A hero worshipped by fans is a near-god, and in mythology the half-divine offspring of a god and a mortal bear the same title.

clue.text: Representing grin of cat in new production

indicators.note: a new production restages the same material differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for the grinning Cheshire Cat in a new stage version of Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatrical picture fits the answer, but 'new production' is the anagram signal, rearranging GRINOFCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To act for someone is to represent them or stand as their deputy.

clue.text: Move vessel to end of dock boundary

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of dock

parts.note: an edge is a boundary or border

explanation.surface: A sailor manoeuvres the ship over to the far edge of the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: To kedge is to move a ship by hauling on a small anchor dropped ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedging is a nautical term for warping a ship forward by hauling on a light anchor.

clue.text: Stamp-on up-market request cut short

indicators.note: in a down light, up says the market word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: cut short means the request word loses its last letter

parts.note: a plea is a request

explanation.surface: An upmarket customer's request is rudely trampled on and cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns MART into TRAM; 'cut short' docks PLEA to PLE. 'Up-market' looks like one adjective, but 'up' is the indicator and 'market' is the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp on something is to crush it underfoot, which is a synonym.

clue.text: It may be described as an electrical discharge

definitions.meaning: in geometry one describes, or draws, a curved segment of a circle with compasses
a luminous flow of current leaping across a gap between electrodes

explanation.definitionFit: Geometers describe a curve of this kind, and a spark bridging two electrodes has the same name.

clue.text: Plant Tom in theatre, in full view

definitions.meaning: a vegetable whose spears are eaten

definitions.text: Tom in theatre, in full view
definitions.meaning: in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum poems Gus the Theatre Cat, a tom, is really named this in full

explanation.walkthrough: Eliot's poem says Gus, the cat at the theatre door, has a longer real name; 'in full' asks for that name, not the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is a plant, and in Eliot's verse the full name of Gus the Theatre Cat matches it.

clue.text: Dispute — involving rent among company workers from time to time

indicators.note: among places the reworked letters inside the company-plus-workers pair

parts.note: temps are temporary staff who work intermittently

indicators.note: involving in its old sense of entangling, so the letters of rent are jumbled

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over rent among a firm's temporary staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' scrambles RENT to NTRE, which goes 'among' CO and TEMPS. The office-dispute surface fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means an awkward clash or minor quarrel, so it is a synonym for a disagreement.

clue.text: Daughter on new-fangled diet came down 10%

indicators.note: new-fangled means made in a novel way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter on a trendy diet loses a tenth of her weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just joins D to the anagram ECIMATED of DIET CAME. The definition is fair because the word originally meant killing one in every ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman punishment killed one soldier in ten, so the word literally means reduced by a tenth.

clue.text: Like a bird in a tree

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Someone compares themselves to a bird perched up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan, a bit of crossword vocabulary worth keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar with trembling leaves is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Old educational establishment has to work with new figure

parts.note: a poly, short for polytechnic, was a British college type merged into universities in 1992
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A former polytechnic has to get going with a new figurehead.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-sided plane shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Regular interruptions in marks for written work

definitions.meaning: breaking something at intervals, as applause interrupts a speech
commas, full stops and the like used in writing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both periodic breaks in a flow and the commas and stops of text.

clue.text: Distributing more per sovereign

indicators.note: distributing spreads the letters out and redeals them in another order

explanation.surface: A ruler hands out more to each person.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch ruling an empire is a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Larva found in aquatic plant

definitions.meaning: the aquatic young of a dragonfly or mayfly
a genus of submerged water weeds also takes the name

explanation.definitionFit: Biologists use the water-nymph name for dragonfly larvae, and it is also a water-weed genus.

clue.text: Clumsy six-footer in English cricket side as opener

indicators.note: as opener puts the preceding group in front of the insect at the start

parts.note: taken as written
leg side is one half of a cricket field, the batter's leg side
an insect has six feet, and an ant is one

explanation.surface: A gangly giant is picked to open the batting for England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' looks like a tall batsman, but it is an insect with six legs. 'As opener' puts IN, E and LEG ahead of ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or polish is clumsiness, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Fighter pilot meeting the force of gravity

parts.note: to fly a plane is to pilot it
weight is the force gravity exerts on a mass

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot copes with the pull of gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter pilot' reads as one RAF phrase, but the fighter is the definition, a boxer in the lightest weight class.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer in the lightest professional weight class is a type of fighter.

clue.text: Forming parts of sea, yet dry in recent past

indicators.note: the letters are taken apart and formed into something new

explanation.surface: Land once part of the sea is now dry, as of late.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today is the most recent past day.

clue.text: Riches like an ancient city engulfed in ashes, say, can produce

indicators.note: engulfed in places the comparison word and city inside the timber word

parts.note: ash trees are an example of trees, hence say
as means like
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Like Pompeii buried under ash, an ancient city can yield riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ashes' points to volcanic ash and a buried city, but it means ash trees: TREES. 'Can produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoards of precious objects are riches or wealth.

clue.text: One who detects exponent of gamesmanship?

definitions.meaning: someone who notices or picks out things, like a talent scout
Stephen Potter wrote the 1947 book Gamesmanship; his initial and surname run together, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter's book 'Gamesmanship' (1947) taught winning by ploys; his initial and surname run together give the second reading, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter picks things out, and the gamesmanship author's name with his initial gives the same letters.

clue.text: During time of prosperity son makes a boob

indicators.note: during says the son letter comes within the boom period

parts.note: a boom is a time of economic prosperity

explanation.surface: In the good times, a son makes a costly blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boob' looks like a mistake, but it is slang for a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal terms for a woman's breast.

clue.text: One of the herd in New York City

definitions.meaning: a bison, a beast that roams in herds
a city in New York State on Lake Erie

explanation.walkthrough: 'New York City' tempts you toward Manhattan, but it means a city in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison of the American plains goes by this name, as does a large city in upstate New York.

clue.text: Mature pine lasting many years

parts.note: to age is to mature
to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A pine tree reaches maturity over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree, but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that endures through ages is long-lasting, a synonym.

clue.text: Girl who welcomes guest vocally?

indicators.note: vocally says the word is spoken and the entry matches its sound

parts.note: a greeter is one who welcomes guests at the door

explanation.surface: A hostess greets a visitor out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Impressions produced by lighting and sound

definitions.text: Impressions produced by lighting and sound

parts.words: Impressions produced by lighting and sound
parts.note: the theatrical illusions created by the lighting and sound crews

explanation.definitionFit: Stage illusions from lamps and speakers are called special lighting and sound effects.

clue.text: Plant is cold place for workers

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a hive houses worker bees

explanation.surface: A factory is a chilly place for its workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, but it is the herb; the 'workers' are bees.
explanation.definitionFit: The onion-flavoured herb is a plant.

clue.text: Unsuitable paint replaced

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Unsuitable paint has to be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not apt, i.e. not fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Winning each rook in last part of chess game

indicators.note: in puts the each-and-rook letters inside the endgame word

parts.note: the ending, or endgame, is the final phase of a game of chess
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A player wins by using each rook in the endgame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' looks like victory at chess, but it means charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile is a charming one, so winning means charming or lovable.

clue.text: Fish found in Georgia left, right and centre

indicators.note: the letters on the left and right edges of Georgia, its first and last
centre picks the middle letter of the seven-letter state name

explanation.surface: A fish turns up all over Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left, right and centre' reads as 'everywhere', but it takes Georgia's first, last and middle letters in that order. The printed clue lacks its letter count (3).
explanation.definitionFit: The garfish, a long-snouted predator, is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Head teachers' organisation

definitions.meaning: slang for the head, as in use your noggin
the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the skull, and the initials of Britain's National Union of Teachers.

clue.text: Money to accept without fitting preparation

parts.note: ready, or the readies, is British slang for cash
taken as written
to wear an idea is to accept or tolerate it, as in he won't wear that

explanation.surface: Cash is offered to make someone accept something without proper preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear' meaning accept is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg clothes are sold finished, not tailored by fitting to the buyer.
